title: Lowercasing a Turkish İ does not give you plain "i"
assumption: Lowercasing a capital letter and comparing it to the obvious ASCII spelling works the way it does for A-Z.

input.display: "\u0130stanbul" (capital I with dot above, U+0130) vs "istanbul"
input.description: A user from Turkey types their city, or their own name, into a search box or signup form that lowercases input to build a case-insensitive lookup key.

what_goes_wrong: "\u0130stanbul".lower() is not "istanbul" — it becomes "i\u0307stanbul" (9 code points instead of 8), so the case-insensitive match against the plain spelling fails, and NFC normalization does not repair it.
why: Python's str.lower() and JavaScript's toLowerCase() apply Unicode's default, locale-independent case mapping. The default lowercase of U+0130 (LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE) is two code points, U+0069 U+0307 ("i" plus COMBINING DOT ABOVE), so the dot is preserved without knowing whether the text is Turkish. Turkish and Azerbaijani pair İ with i and I with ı (dotless), which needs a locale-specific mapping: JavaScript has one in toLocaleLowerCase("tr"), which returns plain "istanbul" here, but Python's str methods take no locale. There is no precomposed lowercase "i with dot above" (i already has a dot), so NFC normalization afterwards does not collapse the pair back to plain "i".

repros.code:
import unicodedata
s = "\u0130stanbul"
lowered = s.lower()
print(lowered, len(s), len(lowered))
print(lowered == "istanbul")
print(unicodedata.normalize("NFC", lowered) == "istanbul")

fix: Do not build a uniqueness or search key by calling lower()/upper() on raw user text when the content may be Turkish or Azerbaijani. When you know the locale, use locale-aware mapping (toLocaleLowerCase("tr") in JavaScript, ICU case mapping with locale "tr"/"az" in Python via a third-party binding). When you do not, use casefold() consistently on both sides, and accept that İ/I/ı/i cannot be folded correctly for every language at once.

sources.title: Unicode Standard: SpecialCasing.txt (default vs. Turkish/Azeri case mappings)

test_cases.note: Any case-insensitive key should unify these two (casefold() does). Whether "İstanbul" should also match plain "istanbul" depends on the locale: yes under Turkish rules, no under the default mapping.
